full_judgment:
2. The plaintiff brought a suit for declaration that the order of the Circle Officer, Revenue in Misc. Case No. 110 of 1973-74 under PO NO.88 of 1972 was illegal and without jurisdiction. In that suit the plaintiff prayed for temporary injunction. 

 3. The trial Court allowed the prayer for temporary injunction and on appeal the same was affirmed. In revision the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division set aside the order of temporary injunction on the finding that the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court having held in the case of Bangladesh Vs. Haji Abdul Gani Biswas and others reported in 32 DLR (AD) 233 that the provisions of PO No. 88 of 1972, PO No. 136 of 1972 and PO No. 24 of 1973 as valid laws, the order of temporary injunction could not be maintained. 

 6. From the judgment of the High Court Division it appears that the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division had not said a word with regard to the alleged unregistered Ekrarnama on consideration of which the courts below granted temporary injunction in favour of the plaintiff. The trial Court found that the alleged unregistered Ekrarnama was not executed on the same day when the kabala was registered. The lower appellate Court upheld this finding of fact and further held that whether the plaintiffs predecessor executed the alleged unregistered Ekramama in favour of the predecessor of the defendants could only be determined at the hearing of the suit on merit. It is needless to say that the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division while setting aside the order of temporary injunction was required to consider this finding of fact of the two courts below. But the being no consideration of this aspect in the case we set aside the impugn judgment and grant temporary injunction till disposal of the suit
